assessment: All findings listed in the initial audit have been remediated in source or build configuration. Registry dependency advisory scans are clean. GLib uses a verified local safety backport; generic version-only scanners still identify its unchanged upstream version.
scope: Tracked Rust and TypeScript/JavaScript source, build scripts, Cargo/pnpm manifests and lockfiles, Tauri capabilities/CSP/updater settings, CI and Arch packaging.
Targeted searches and review for persistence, process injection/writes, credential theft, network uploads, obfuscated execution, install hooks, unsafe URL opening and path traversal.
Windows Defender custom scan of the project directory, with remediation disabled.
npm advisory audit, OSV queries for every locked Rust registry package, and npm integrity verification for every locked JavaScript package.

malware_scan.result: Final custom project scan completed with exit code 0: found no threats.
malware_scan.signature_freshness: Read from Defender during final validation; signature updated within the preceding 24 hours.

changes: Pinned all direct Rust registry dependencies with exact = versions and all direct JavaScript dependencies with exact versions; synchronized pnpm specifiers without changing resolved JavaScript packages.
Updated tokio 1.53.2 to 1.53.3, rustls 0.23.45 to 0.23.46, rustls-webpki 0.103.15 to 0.103.16, webpki-roots 1.0.9 to 1.0.10, and webpki-root-certs 1.0.9 to 1.0.10.
Removed the unused legacy ZIP updater feature, eliminating zip 4.6.1 and its advisory findings. Current release metadata uses raw EXE/MSI/AppImage/DEB/RPM assets.
Restricted the Rust open_url command to parsed HTTP/HTTPS URLs without embedded credentials, preventing OS file and custom protocol handler launches from untrusted links.
Restricted webview navigation to the configured local application and development origins, including scheme and port checks.
Pinned seven distinct GitHub Actions to verified upstream commit SHAs and the Arch build container to a verified registry digest.
Pinned Node 24.15.0 in .node-version and CI, retained existing pnpm 10.29.3 and Rust 1.98.1 pins, and pinned the editor Rust formatter instead of using nightly.
Added frozen/locked build instructions and Cargo flags in release, packaging and type-generation scripts; added app/.npmrc save-exact=true.
Limited the default workflow token to contents:read and supplied updater signing secrets only to build/signing steps.
Added pnpm deps:check and ran it in release builds to enforce application dependency pins, lockfile agreement, action SHAs, container digests and exact toolchain versions.
Applied the four remediations recorded in resolved_findings, and corrected both existing tests to normalize Windows CRLF line endings.
Added exact per-file vendor hashes and small upstream-relative review patches under vendor/patches; the pin check rejects source drift.
Replaced the deleted continuous AppImage tool asset with numbered release 1.9.1 and its verified SHA-256 hash.
Updated privacy documentation for credential-store migration and actual authentication/webhook traffic.
Arch packaging now consumes an exact clean-checkout source archive with a mandatory SHA-256 checksum, rather than downloading the old unpatched release. Dirty checkouts and SKIP hashes are rejected.

limitations: The audit is a targeted code, dependency and malware review, not a proof that every line of all upstream code is benign.
Published upstream installers, signing infrastructure, live game services and the already-running app were not replaced or independently audited.
No GitHub release was published; hosted CI execution, Arch package execution and production updater signing/delivery were not end-to-end exercised.
OS snapshot packages were frozen and authenticated by their distribution package manager; a separate native-OS CVE database scan was not performed.

resolved_findings.resolution: Backported upstream commit b5a4071e439bef2b5eea76c3aa25e5ae84839e34 to verified glib 0.18.5 source. Both forward and reverse string iteration pass the Linux regression test with the GLib library compiled at opt-level=2. The original version is retained, and the complete reviewed source and patch hashes are enforced.

Removed proc-macro-error, proc-macro-error2, zvariant, zvariant_derive and zbus_names from the resolved graph. GTK macros use maintained proc-macro-error3 3.1.1 with Syn 2 support. Notifications and file-manager integration use the supported native dbus 0.9.12 backend. Native notification delivery remains async to callers, with its connection retained on a worker thread.

Tokens now use Windows Credential Manager with local-machine persistence, or Linux Secret Service with encrypted D-Bus communication. No new plaintext fallback is written. Legacy file/JSON copies migrate only after a verified secure write; logout removes both formats. Unavailable keyrings leave the app usable anonymously and report login-save errors without leaking backend secret bytes.

Linux builds use a digest-pinned Ubuntu builder, a signed dated package snapshot and hash-verified Rust/Node/pnpm/CA archives. Arch uses a digest-pinned container and fixed archive date. Windows checks its exact hosted image revision and refuses unreviewed drift. Eight native tool archives/assets have SHA-256 checks, use a private cache and are verified before execution. Linux bundling was tested with networking disabled; Windows blocks further GitHub helper downloads. Installers require the OS WebView2 runtime rather than fetching a bootstrapper.

review_notes: GLib version 0.18.5 is intentionally retained. Its generic upstream advisory is addressed by the reviewed patch, not by changing a version number or globally suppressing the advisory.

Existing plaintext tokens migrate when the rebuilt app next accesses an unlocked OS credential store. A failed migration preserves the old token rather than silently losing it; anonymous operation continues until the store is available.

Standard GitHub-hosted Windows jobs cannot request historical image revisions. The exact-image guard intentionally stops releases after image rotation until pins are reviewed or a matching self-hosted runner is used.

Public game feeds and OS-managed runtimes remain live runtime inputs. Memory access remains read-only; authenticated requests go to warframe.market and optional notifications go to the configured webhook.
Unrelated buff/timer changes were edited concurrently. They were preserved. Validation numbers below describe the tested source snapshots, not a promise about later edits in the shared workspace.
